title: Chicken Enchilada Suiza Spoon Bake
description: Soft corn tortillas soak up a mild tomatillo cream sauce in a covered chicken bake finished with Monterey Jack.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: plain cooked mild poblano pepper
ingredients.note: Peeled and seeded, with ribs removed.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

ingredients.name: soft corn tortillas
ingredients.note: Use small six-inch tortillas. Tear into small soft pieces.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the Samsung oven to 350°F on conventional Bake with the middle rack in place.

steps.title: Simmer the tomatillos
steps.text: In the lidded HexClad, simmer {tomatillos}, {pepper}, {cumin} and {broth} for 8–12 minutes until the tomatillos are soft and dull green.

steps.title: Smooth the green sauce
steps.text: Blend the hot vegetables and liquid in a deep heatproof jug. Pass through a fine sieve back into the HexClad to catch skin and seeds.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} until completely smooth.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Enrich the sauce
steps.text: Off heat, whisk {cream} into the warm green sauce until completely smooth.

steps.title: Layer the spoon bake
steps.text: Spread a thin layer of sauce in the casserole. Cut {chicken} into short 1/2-inch pieces. Layer the chicken and {tortillas} loosely in the dish, coating each layer with sauce and finishing with a generous layer of sauce.

steps.title: Bake until tender
steps.text: Cover and bake for 20–30 minutes, checking from 18 minutes. Probe several of the thickest chicken pieces for 175°F and check the center of the bake for at least 165°F.

steps.title: Melt the Jack
steps.text: Scatter {jack} over the steaming sauce and replace the lid for 3 minutes until the cheese melts.

steps.title: Sauce and serve
steps.text: Spoon into four shallow bowls while the tortillas are soft, drawing sauce from the edges over each portion.

notes: Sauce yield: About 3 cups of sauce before layering. The tortillas soften in it and the finished bake stays spoonable. Make ahead: Cook and strain the tomatillo base a day ahead. Bring it to a simmer before thickening and assembling the casserole. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The tortillas are meant to be soft and the sauce protects the chicken. Freeze covered portions for up to 6 weeks. Fridge reheat: Spoon one portion and its sauce into a small covered oven-safe dish. Warm at 325°F on conventional Bake, checking after 15 minutes, until the coldest center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses tomatillos and mild poblano. For gentler Option B, substitute cooked peeled zucchini for the tomatillos by weight and peeled sweet bell pepper for the poblano by volume. For a dairy-free bake, replace the cream cheese with unsweetened oat cream and omit the Jack. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 327 kcal, 33.4 g protein, 21.1 g total carbohydrate, 11.9 g fat, 3.0 g fiber, 240 mg sodium. Includes all the chicken and sauce in the listed recipe. Sodium varies with the broth. Fiber is estimated before straining.
